free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: No account needed to start (25 GB per file without one).

retention.stated: Retention: 15 days anonymous, 90 days from last download for a free account, never for Contributor/Plus
retention.notes: Links last 90 days after the last download · 15 without an account

egress.terms: No ads, no wait, no cap, full speed on every plan; no per-download bandwidth meter stated. Bytes are served from R2/B2 origins via short-lived signed URLs.

tooling: Own REST API, documented and keyless for the anonymous path. /api/upload/create, /api/upload/part, /api/upload/complete. Remote-upload endpoint POST /api/upload/remote pulls a URL server-side (no local bandwidth).
chaining: Anonymous upload needs no key at all, so per-identity multiplication is free; but each anon file lives only 15 days from last download. The interesting route is the automatic Contributor tier: park 25 GB, wait 30 days, and links stop expiring (100 GB). A slow-burn archive, not a hot tier.
limits_note: per-object-cap: 25 GB/file anonymous, 50 GB/file free account. Retention: 15 days anonymous, 90 days from last download for a free account, never for Contributor/Plus. Storage cap is the real bind: 50 GB free account, 100 GB Contributor, 5 TB only on the invite-only Verified tier.

reliability_note: READ PATH IS GATED BY A MINTED TOKEN, not a static URL: /d/<id> is HTML whose Download button is a signed /dl/<JWT> that 302s to an R2 presigned URL with X-Amz-Expires=21600. The token is re-minted on every page view, so the file is durable but the *link* is not shareable as a bytes URL. You must re-scrape /d/<id> to fetch. Retains originals byte-exact.
